references.text: God reminds Jacob of the promise he made in Bethel and commands him to return there.
God instructs Jacob to return to Bethel, and Jacob acknowledges God's faithfulness by recalling the promise He gave him there.
God renews His blessing over Jacob in Bethel, the place where Jacob first made his vow.
Israel makes a conditional vow (neder) to the Lord ('if you give... then I will...'), parallel to Jacob's vow at Bethel.
The law that whoever makes a vow to the Lord must keep their word – relevant for Jacob's neder.
The command to fulfill vows made to the Lord, emphasizing the seriousness of a neder like Jacob's.
Jephthah's vow to the Lord follows the same conditional structure as Jacob's vow: 'if you give... then I will...'
Paul's exhortation to be content with food and clothing reflects Jacob's simple prayer for bread to eat and garments to wear.
Thematic parallel: Two prayers with a conditional structure ('if you...') where the person seeks God's presence and protection as the basis for life's needs.
Narrative connection: The vow made at Bethel (28) is actively invoked and confirmed by Jacob upon his return (32), showing continuity in God's promise.
Literary and theological parallel: Both verses show patriarchs (Jacob) praying for God's blessing on their journey before leaving home.
Vow and confirmation: Jacob's prayer that God would be with him (28) is directly confirmed by the Lord in 31:3.
